prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
**[goal]** A single-file landing page for Mondrian's *Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow* (1930), built only on `FACTSHEET.md`.

**[action]** Created `landing/index.html`: one self-contained file, no build step, no JS. Header is a Mondrian grid (white ground, 14px black lines, red/blue/yellow cells) carrying the title, painter, year, medium and collection. Sections: The Painter (Mondrian 1872–1944, Dutch, co-founded De Stijl with van Doesburg in 1917), The Movement (Neoplasticism principles as three colour blocks: lines, colours, non-colours), The Picture (red square top right, blue bottom left, yellow rectangle bottom right, thick black lines), Why It Matters (asymmetric balance as reference for graphic design and architecture). Footer invites the visitor to read more via a link to the Wikipedia source URL. Google Fonts (Archivo) is the only external request; the three.js CDN was not needed and is unused.

**[result]** Opened the file directly in the browser (`file://`) and screenshotted it top, middle and bottom: grid renders, fonts load, no console-visible breakage, responsive collapse handled at 760px. Every claim on the page was checked line-by-line against `FACTSHEET.md`; I also removed one sentence of interpretation that went beyond the facts, so the page now asserts nothing the fact sheet doesn't state.

**[next]** None. Assumptions stated: English copy, the exact Wikipedia URL as the read-more source, colours chosen to evoke the work (the fact sheet gives no hex values), and no reproduction of the painting itself (not required by the brief and possibly restricted).
checks: has a page title and an h1
names the painting (Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow)
links to the fact sheet's source
CSS with the Mondrian palette (red, blue, yellow, black)
